name: MoSPI: IIP, WPI, NAS, CPI (reference)
note_why: A reference pipeline (signals/README, MoSPI; COMPOSITION_SPEC §24): saved releases, a consolidated CSV and a gate, but no compute module, no skeleton, no system model and no signals of its own. Its only consumer is the 1f family on the credit pipelines that declare depends_on: ["mospi"]. order 0 because a pipeline's order must come after everything it depends on (test_manifest), and every credit pipeline may depend on this one.

api.note_why: page_size: 200 is the largest the API accepts (300 → HTTP 400, probed 2026-09-28 on all three endpoints). The server needs TLS legacy renegotiation, which OpenSSL 3 refuses by default; mospi_api enables it for this host only.

iip.note_why: Lag: July 2026 was released 28 Aug (MoSPI calendar: the 28th of M+1).
iip.note_tests_read: The driver and arrow tests read iip_2011: this base starts after the credit history (Oct 2021), and switching bases mid-series puts a step in every growth series (IIP trailing-year output: median gap 1.8 points, measured 2026-10-21). Revisit when this base holds the test window on its own (~2028).
iip.note_driver: growth/driver_measure/tide: how the driver test reads this dataset (signals/README "RBI lending and deposit rates": declared per dataset, never defaulted). An index changes by ratio; its tide is its own headline, so 'prices rose in general' is not read as this series moving.

wpi.note_printed_growth: WPI prints no growth rate on the API: every WPI series is counted as no_printed_rate.
wpi.note_why: base_year=2022-23 is UNDOCUMENTED and load-bearing: without it the API serves the 2011-12 series with status 200. The 953 items (rows with `item` set, ~85% of the volume) are dropped at fetch because nothing reads them: a declared decision, not an accident. Lag: August 2026 was released 14 Sep.
wpi.note_tests_read: The driver and arrow tests read wpi_2011: this base starts after the credit history (Oct 2021), and switching bases mid-series puts a step in every growth series (IIP trailing-year output: median gap 1.8 points, measured 2026-10-21). Revisit when this base holds the test window on its own (~2028).

nic:10/sugar.why: The 2011-12 base has no sugar index, only sugar, molasses & honey: its monthly change tracks current-base sugar at r 0.91 (Apr 2024 - Apr 2026, measured 2026-10-25). User-approved 2026-10-25.

nic:24/basic_iron_and_steel.why: The 2011-12 base splits steel into seven sub-groups and prints no iron & steel total; adding them needs weights we do not invent. Basic metals (steel plus non-ferrous) stands in: its monthly change tracks iron & steel at r 0.96 on the current base and 0.83 across bases (measured 2026-10-25).

wpi.note_tests_approximate: A code the test base lacks is read from a declared stand-in on that base; every result that uses one names it (`approximated`).

nas.note_no_printed_rate: MoSPI prints quarterly growth only for GVA (indicator 21) and GDP (22); indicators 1-34 enumerated 2026-09-28. PFCE is counted as no_printed_rate.
nas.note_why: frequency_code is honoured; `frequency` is silently ignored (282 rows, annual mixed in), which is why every filter is verified on the rows. Without base_year one response mixes both bases. The growth indicators (21, 22) carry the printed rate in the price columns. Lag: Q1 FY27 was released 29 Aug.

annex_xlsx.note_why: The press release's own Excel annex in MoSPI's eSankhyiki catalogue, fetched automatically (cpi_annex.py). One table holds the base-2024 Combined index from Jan 2025, MoSPI's printed inflation from Jan 2026, and the provisional mark. Selected by its title, which states the base, never by annex number: 'Annex-IV' was a base-2012 state table until Dec 2025. Every listed release is saved (sha256 dedupes), so a missed month is recovered on the next run. Catalogue entries for Feb–Aug 2026 were all created 2026-10-01: measured on September's release (12 Oct): not listed by 18 Oct, so the annex is the later confirmation, not the release-day source.

release_pdf.note_why: The monthly press release, the release-day source. September 2026 settled it (PLAN): the annex was not listed by 18 Oct, 6 days after the 12 Oct release, so the PDF stays. Read with `fetch.py --cpi-pdf`; MoSPI's product feed (www.mospi.gov.in/api/product/get-product-data, product 9) lists every release PDF with its path, a candidate for fetching it automatically. Releases Jan-Sep 2026 saved from it.

dashboard_xlsx.note_why: The 'download data' workbook on MoSPI's CPI page, fetched automatically. It holds the base-2024 index back to Jan 2025, which gives CPI a year back so 1c can check MoSPI's printed inflation against the index. It lags the press release (on 2026-09-28 it still ended in July, dated 12 Aug), states no P/F flag and no base.
dashboard_xlsx.retired: 2026-10-18 (user): redundant with the press-release PDF (release day) and the eSankhyiki annex (later), and no longer dated by its name: the file named 12.09.2026 was updated in October to hold September. Not fetched; copies saved before stay as history.

cpi.note_max_revision: A revision beyond 1% of the value fails. CPI revisions are ~0.01 index points (Jan 2026: 104.46 → 104.45); the workbook states no base, so a level jump between the two publications (a 2012-base series is ~200) must stop the run rather than warn.
cpi.note_why: The API holds only the 2012 base, ending Dec 2025 (base_year=2024 → 'No Data Found', re-probed 2026-09-28); it is never used. CPI is one dataset fed by two MoSPI publications (`sources`). Their releases merge in PUBLICATION order (`published`), not fetch order, because the workbook lags: fetched after the August release, it would otherwise overwrite July's final value with the provisional one. Lag: July 2026 was released 12 Aug.
cpi.note_tests_read: The driver and arrow tests read cpi_2012: this base starts after the credit history (Oct 2021), and switching bases mid-series puts a step in every growth series (IIP trailing-year output: median gap 1.8 points, measured 2026-10-21). Revisit when this base holds the test window on its own (~2028).

iip_2011.note_why: A retired base, read only by the driver and arrow tests (`tests_read` on the current dataset; signals/README "Longer history", user 2026-10-21): one series on one base from Oct 2021, never linked to the current base. Fetched once: a release is saved only while none reaching `final_period` exists. Rows before `from_period` are not consolidated: Nov 2019 is the earliest month a test from Oct 2021 can read (a change one month apart of a YoY, at a delay of up to 9 months). Old-base growth is printed (growth_rate), so 1c checks it.

growth_published.2021-04-30: MoSPI printed no growth for Apr 2021, on any of its 33 groups, against the lockdown month Apr 2020: its blank, not a hole in our data.

wpi_2011.note_why: A retired base, read only by the driver and arrow tests (`tests_read` on the current dataset; signals/README "Longer history", user 2026-10-21): one series on one base from Oct 2021, never linked to the current base. Fetched once: a release is saved only while none reaching `final_period` exists. Rows before `from_period` are not consolidated: Nov 2019 is the earliest month a test from Oct 2021 can read (a change one month apart of a YoY, at a delay of up to 9 months). Requested a year at a time from 2019: the base holds 146,861 rows from 2012, ~85% items (dropped, as on the current base).
wpi_2011.note_workers: MoSPI answered HTTP 429 at 6 parallel requests over ~400 pages (2026-10-25).

cpi_2012.note_why: A retired base, read only by the driver and arrow tests (`tests_read` on the current dataset; signals/README "Longer history", user 2026-10-21): one series on one base from Oct 2021, never linked to the current base. Fetched once: a release is saved only while none reaching `final_period` exists. Rows before `from_period` are not consolidated: Nov 2019 is the earliest month a test from Oct 2021 can read (a change one month apart of a YoY, at a delay of up to 9 months). The API's only CPI base; rows carry `baseyear`, not `base_year` (base_field). One row a month: all-India, combined, general index.

inflation_published.2020-04-30: No inflation was printed for Apr-May 2020: price collection was suspended in the lockdown.

note_currency_stage: The stage a dependent's gate runs first (core/gate.py, depends_on): the release calendar, so no credit pipeline computes 1f against MoSPI data that is overdue.
note_grace: Days past the declared lag before a missing period is overdue. MoSPI moves a release off a weekend (CPI for Aug 2026, nominally the 12th, came on the 15th), and releases land at 4 PM.
